eval.title: Verizon Stock (VZ) Intrinsic Value

call.headline_quote: fairly priced at the moment for a 10% return

base_metric.name: dps
base_metric.quote: the dividend I have already put it in here the dividend is $2.6 per share

scenarios.name: normal
scenarios.quote: the intrinsic value is 3835 close to the stock price so fairly valued for a 10% return

scenarios.name: best
scenarios.quote: suddenly the required dividend yield is 5% somewhere in the future then you immediately see Verizon going to 50

scenarios.name: worst
scenarios.quote: if there is no growth going forward but still the dividend remains and the dividend yield goes to 8% on higher rates then the present value sum is much higher

what_is_priced_in.quote: there is always a let's say 300 basis point premium yield on the let's say risk-free yield there from Verizon that is how the thing is priced

reasons.claim: At current price Verizon offers a fair, roughly 10% expected return from dividend plus modest growth.
reasons.quote: fairly priced at the moment for a 10% return

data_check.gap_note: he says 38.35, as-of 28.51 (T0); annual vs TTM or a different definition; not in our data: discount rate

reasons.claim: Verizon is essentially an interest-rate proxy: rising rates push up the required dividend yield and debt refinancing costs, pushing the stock down, and vice versa.
reasons.quote: when interest rates go up Verizon stock goes down on the other hand when interest rates go down everything looks better for Verizon

data_check.gap_note: he says 0.0429, as-of 0.0676209 (FY2023); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: The large debt pile and rising refinancing costs are the persistent anchor and main risk on the stock.
reasons.quote: this is refinancing in 2025 and 0.85 is the interest rates now going forward the interest cost there will be 5% so that's six times higher interest payment

data_check.gap_note: he says 1.5e+11, as-of 1.74942e+11 (FY2023); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: Revenue is essentially flat and growth is limited by a highly competitive market where T-Mobile keeps taking share.
reasons.quote: the total revenue we can say it flat as a pancake that is what Verizon has been able to deliver

data_check.gap_note: trajectory visible at T0; no number stated

reasons.claim: A forced dividend cut to manage debt would collapse the intrinsic value, the key downside risk.
reasons.quote: if they are forced to cut it to 1.5 then you see the present value now would go to below 20 that is the key risk

data_check.gap_note: he says 20, as-of 28.51 (T0); annual vs TTM or a different definition

external_facts_used: Frontier fiber acquisition for about 20 billion, said to be immediately accretive to EBITDA
Verizon has invested about 200 billion over the last 10 years in 5G spectrum and fiber
40-year bond issued at 3.73% for five billion
